key_insight: BetaMem gives embodied agents traceable, evolving long-term memory by combining grounded memory writing, failure-driven rule repair, and budget-aware storage and retrieval.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets more reliable long-horizon agents while controlling memory growth, retrieval costs, and repeated mistakes.
method: Links six memory layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural.
Uses supervised fine-tuning and teacher-verified reinforcement learning to enforce executable, source-supported memory writes.
Repairs memory policies through causal failure diagnosis and independent replay checks, with budget-aware tools for storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting.
evidence_signal: With Qwen3.5-9B, BetaMem reports leading scores among listed memory methods on four benchmarks; training raises write-contract compliance from 50.9% to 86.2% and reduces output tokens per stored action by 47.3%.
watch_item: Results use benchmark-specific evaluation protocols, and teacher verification plus replay checks may add implementation and compute overhead.
paper_title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
